What to record: Identify the released project, material batch, and cut-list revision.
Record who set up and ran the process plus the production date.
Identify machine, blade, bit, cutter, jig, or program version.
State the face, edge, fence, stop, datum, or coordinate origin.
Example: Show face up / factory left edge

What to record: Record hole IDs, coordinates or spacing, origin, face, and handedness.
Record diameter, point style, stop setting, backer, and breakthrough rule.
Record test panel, first and last hole positions, depth, and hardware fit.
Record interval panel, jig cleaning, stop changes, and suspect parts.
Example: Verify first of each cabinet side pair
